explanation_en: In informal Portuguese, 'bancar' means to pay for, finance, or foot the bill for something (like a trip, a meal, or an event). It can also mean 'to act like' or 'to pretend to be' (e.g., 'bancar o bobo'), but here it refers to financial backing.

examples.en_text: My parents are going to foot the bill for my vacation trip to the beach.
examples.target_text: Meus pais vão bancar a minha viagem de férias para a praia.

examples.en_text: Don't worry about dinner, I'll pay for everything today.
examples.target_text: Não se preocupe com o jantar, eu banco tudo hoje.

examples.en_text: The company decided to foot the bill for all the employees' English course.
examples.target_text: A empresa decidiu bancar o curso de inglês de todos os funcionários.

examples.en_text: He footed the bill for our entire trip and didn't want to receive anything back.
examples.target_text: Ele bancou toda a nossa viagem e não quis receber nada de volta.

examples.en_text: Who is going to foot the bill for such an expensive birthday party?
examples.target_text: Quem vai bancar essa festa de aniversário tão cara?

examples.en_text: They are looking for an investor to fund the new project.
examples.target_text: Eles estão procurando um investidor para bancar o novo projeto.

explanation_en: 'Aliviar' means to ease or relieve, but when paired with 'para' and a person, it means to go easy on someone, show leniency, or let them off the hook. It is highly common in legal, political, and personal contexts.

examples.en_text: Teacher, go easy on me, I had to work late yesterday and couldn't study.
examples.target_text: Professor, alivia aí para mim, eu tive que trabalhar até tarde ontem e não consegui estudar.

examples.en_text: The boss went easy on João because he knew he was going through personal problems.
examples.target_text: O chefe aliviou aí para o João porque sabia que ele estava passando por problemas pessoais.

examples.en_text: Mom, go easy on my brother, he didn't do it on purpose.
examples.target_text: Mãe, alivia aí para o meu irmão, ele não fez de propósito.

examples.en_text: I hope the coach goes easy on us in today's practice, it's very hot.
examples.target_text: Espero que o treinador alivie aí para nós no treino de hoje, está muito quente.

examples.en_text: Please, officer, go easy on me this time, I really didn't see the sign.
examples.target_text: Por favor, policial, alivia aí para mim dessa vez, eu realmente não vi a placa.

examples.en_text: If you don't go easy on your son, he will end up being afraid to talk to you.
examples.target_text: Se você não aliviar aí para o seu filho, ele vai acabar ficando com medo de falar com você.

explanation_en: "Ter receio" is a common and slightly more formal alternative to "ter medo" (to be afraid). It is widely used in both spoken and written Portuguese to express apprehension or hesitation. It is typically followed by the preposition "de" and an infinitive or noun.

examples.en_text: Were you afraid of changing jobs after so many years at the same company?
examples.target_text: Você teve receio de mudar de emprego depois de tantos anos na mesma empresa?

examples.en_text: She was afraid of speaking in public because her Portuguese was not yet perfect.
examples.target_text: Ela teve receio de falar em público porque o seu português ainda não estava perfeito.

examples.en_text: João was afraid of traveling alone through Europe, but everything went well.
examples.target_text: O João teve receio de viajar sozinho pela Europa, mas correu tudo bem.

examples.en_text: Were you afraid of investing your money in that new project?
examples.target_text: Você teve receio de investir o seu dinheiro naquele novo projeto?

examples.en_text: He was afraid of asking his colleagues for help when the work got difficult.
examples.target_text: Ele teve receio de pedir ajuda aos colegas quando o trabalho ficou difícil.

examples.en_text: Maria was afraid of going to the doctor, but the exam was very quick.
examples.target_text: A Maria teve receio de ir ao médico, mas o exame foi muito rápido.

explanation_en: "Ter ideia" is frequently used in negative sentences ("não ter ideia") to mean "to have no clue" or "to not know at all." It is a very natural conversational expression in Portuguese. It is usually followed by "de" or "de que."

examples.en_text: I had no idea that the museum was closed on Mondays.
examples.target_text: Eu não tinha ideia de que o museu fechava às segundas-feiras.

examples.en_text: Did you have any idea how much this computer cost before the discount?
examples.target_text: Tu tinhas ideia de quanto custava este computador antes do desconto?

examples.en_text: She had the idea of opening a small restaurant, but she changed her plans.
examples.target_text: Ela tinha ideia de abrir um pequeno restaurante, mas mudou de planos.

examples.en_text: We had no idea that the meeting was going to be so long.
examples.target_text: Nós não tínhamos ideia de que a reunião ia ser tão longa.

examples.en_text: They already had an idea of what they wanted to do over the weekend.
examples.target_text: Eles já tinham ideia do que queriam fazer no fim de semana.

examples.en_text: I had the impression that we already knew each other from somewhere.
examples.target_text: Eu tinha ideia de que nós já nos conhecíamos de algum lado.

explanation_en: "De madrugada" refers to the time between midnight and sunrise, typically between 1 AM and 5 AM. Unlike English, which often uses "at night" or "in the early morning," Portuguese has this specific noun phrase "madrugada" which is used adverbially with "de." It is an essential vocabulary item for daily life.

examples.en_text: I usually wake up in the early hours of the morning to study when the house is quiet.
examples.target_text: Eu costumo acordar de madrugada para estudar quando a casa está silenciosa.

examples.en_text: Our flight to Lisbon leaves in the early hours of the morning, so we have to go to the airport early.
examples.target_text: O nosso voo para Lisboa sai de madrugada, por isso temos de ir cedo para o aeroporto.

examples.en_text: It started raining very hard in the early hours of the morning and the noise woke me up.
examples.target_text: Começou a chover muito forte de madrugada e o barulho acordou-me.

examples.en_text: My brother works in a hospital and usually works shifts in the early hours of the morning.
examples.target_text: O meu irmão trabalha num hospital e costuma fazer turnos de madrugada.

examples.en_text: They got home in the early hours of the morning and tried not to make noise so as not to wake the neighbors.
examples.target_text: Eles chegaram a casa de madrugada e tentaram não fazer barulho para não acordar os vizinhos.

examples.en_text: If you feel sick in the middle of the night, you can call me at any time.
examples.target_text: Se te sentires mal de madrugada, podes ligar-me a qualquer hora.

explanation_en: "Fazer um escândalo" means to make a scene, throw a tantrum, or react very loudly and publicly to something. While "escândalo" translates to "scandal," in this collocation it refers to a loud, dramatic public protest or scene rather than a political scandal.

examples.en_text: She made a scene in the restaurant because the food was cold.
examples.target_text: Ela fez um escândalo no restaurante porque a comida estava fria.

examples.en_text: Please, don't make a scene here in front of everyone.
examples.target_text: Por favor, não faça um escândalo aqui na frente de todo mundo.

examples.en_text: The neighbors made a scene last night because of the noise.
examples.target_text: Os vizinhos fizeram um escândalo ontem à noite por causa do barulho.

examples.en_text: He was afraid of making a scene if he ran into his ex-girlfriend.
examples.target_text: Ele tinha medo de fazer um escândalo se encontrasse a ex-namorada.

examples.en_text: Every time things don't go his way, he makes a scene.
examples.target_text: Toda vez que as coisas não saem do jeito dele, ele faz um escândalo.

examples.en_text: The customer made a scene in the store when they told him he couldn't return the product.
examples.target_text: O cliente fez um escândalo na loja quando disseram que ele não podia devolver o produto.

explanation_en: "No meio da rua" literally means "in the middle of the street," but idiomatically it often means "out in public" or "in the open for everyone to see." It is a very common expression used when describing public scenes, arguments, or unexpected events.

examples.en_text: The car suddenly stopped in the middle of the street.
examples.target_text: O carro parou de repente no meio da rua.

examples.en_text: It started raining hard when I was in the middle of the street.
examples.target_text: Começou a chover muito quando eu estava no meio da rua.

examples.en_text: I ran into my old teacher in the middle of the street and we stood talking.
examples.target_text: Encontrei o meu antigo professor no meio da rua e ficámos a conversar.

examples.en_text: It is very dangerous for children to play in the middle of the street.
examples.target_text: É muito perigoso para as crianças brincarem no meio da rua.

examples.en_text: I dropped my keys in the middle of the street and now I can't find them.
examples.target_text: Eu deixei cair as minhas chaves no meio da rua e agora não as encontro.

examples.en_text: There was a dog lying in the middle of the street, so I had to stop the car.
examples.target_text: Havia um cão deitado no meio da rua, por isso tive de parar o carro.

explanation_en: "Falta de vergonha" is a powerful Portuguese expression used to describe a lack of moral decency, shamelessness, or corruption. It is widely used in political and social commentary to criticize unethical behavior or systemic neglect.

examples.en_text: It is a total lack of shame that they keep lying after everything that happened.
examples.target_text: É uma falta de vergonha que eles continuem a mentir depois de tudo o que aconteceu.

examples.en_text: He had the nerve to ask me to borrow money again.
examples.target_text: Ele teve a falta de vergonha de me pedir dinheiro emprestado outra vez.

examples.en_text: That lack of shame in the middle of the street made everyone uncomfortable.
examples.target_text: Aquela falta de vergonha no meio da rua deixou toda a gente desconfortável.

examples.en_text: Arriving two hours late and not apologizing is incredibly shameless.
examples.target_text: Chegar duas horas atrasado e não pedir desculpa é uma enorme falta de vergonha.

examples.en_text: I can't stand my neighbor's lack of shame anymore, making noise all night.
examples.target_text: Não aguento mais a falta de vergonha do meu vizinho, que faz barulho a noite toda.

examples.en_text: The company director showed a total lack of shame by blaming the employees for the mistake.
examples.target_text: O diretor da empresa mostrou uma total falta de vergonha ao culpar os funcionários pelo erro.

explanation_en: Used to describe a strong, sometimes desperate, desire or eagerness to achieve something. It often carries a connotation of impatience or acting hastily due to this desire. It is typically followed by an infinitive verb.

examples.en_text: In his eagerness to get a promotion, he ended up working late every day.
examples.target_text: Na ânsia de conseguir uma promoção, ele acabou trabalhando até mais tarde todos os dias.

examples.en_text: In their eagerness to see the sea, the children ran to the beach as soon as we arrived at the hotel.
examples.target_text: Na ânsia de ver o mar, as crianças correram para a praia assim que chegamos ao hotel.

examples.en_text: In her eagerness to reply quickly, she ended up sending the message with several typos.
examples.target_text: Na ânsia de responder rapidamente, ela acabou enviando a mensagem com vários erros de digitação.

examples.en_text: In his eagerness to buy the new cell phone, he spent all the money he had saved.
examples.target_text: Na ânsia de comprar o novo celular, ele gastou todo o dinheiro que tinha economizado.

examples.en_text: In her eagerness to defend her point of view, she didn't let anyone else speak during the meeting.
examples.target_text: Na ânsia de defender seu ponto de vista, ela não deixou mais ninguém falar durante a reunião.

examples.en_text: In my eagerness to finish the book quickly, I skipped some important chapters.
examples.target_text: Na ânsia de terminar o livro logo, eu pulei alguns capítulos importantes.

explanation_en: A very common colloquial expression used to emphasize that what one is saying is true, serious, and not a joke. It is equivalent to 'I'm serious' or 'no kidding' in English. It is often used in the first person as 'eu não tô brincando'.

examples.en_text: I'm not joking, the situation at the company is really serious.
examples.target_text: Eu não tô brincando, a situação na empresa está realmente séria.

examples.en_text: Man, I'm not joking, that dog over there actually bites.
examples.target_text: Cara, não tô brincando, aquele cachorro ali morde de verdade.

examples.en_text: You're not joking with me, right? I really need this information.
examples.target_text: Você não tá brincando comigo, né? Eu preciso mesmo dessa informação.

examples.en_text: I'm not joking when I say this is the best cake I've ever eaten.
examples.target_text: Eu não tô brincando quando digo que esse é o melhor bolo que já comi.

examples.en_text: I think you'd better study, because the teacher is not joking about tomorrow's exam.
examples.target_text: Acho melhor você estudar, porque a professora não tá brincando sobre a prova de amanhã.

examples.en_text: I won the lottery! Seriously, I'm not joking, look at the ticket.
examples.target_text: Eu ganhei na loteria! Sério, não tô brincando, olha aqui o bilhete.

explanation_en: A highly common colloquial filler and modifier meaning 'sort of' or 'kind of'. It softens a statement or indicates that something is approximately true. It is extremely frequent in spoken Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.en_text: Today I'm sort of not in the mood to do anything.
examples.target_text: Hoje eu estou meio que sem vontade de fazer nada.

examples.en_text: She was sort of upset about what you said yesterday.
examples.target_text: Ela meio que ficou chateada com o que você disse ontem.

examples.en_text: We sort of already knew that this was going to happen.
examples.target_text: Nós meio que já sabíamos que isso ia acontecer.

examples.en_text: I sort of got lost on the way to the restaurant.
examples.target_text: Eu meio que me perdi no caminho para o restaurante.

examples.en_text: The movie is good, but the ending is sort of confusing.
examples.target_text: O filme é bom, mas o final é meio que confuso.

examples.en_text: I sort of forgot to send that important email.
examples.target_text: Eu meio que esqueci de enviar aquele e-mail importante.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to come to the surface of the water', this idiom is used figuratively to mean that a secret, piece of information, or issue has been revealed or has come to public attention. It is common in journalism and everyday discussions.

examples.en_text: After many years, the truth about the accident finally came to light.
examples.target_text: Depois de muitos anos, a verdade sobre o acidente finalmente veio à tona.

examples.en_text: During the conversation, old childhood memories surfaced.
examples.target_text: Durante a conversa, velhas lembranças da infância vieram à tona.

examples.en_text: The political scandal came to light right after the elections.
examples.target_text: O escândalo político veio à tona logo após as eleições.

examples.en_text: Whenever we argue about money, other problems from the past surface.
examples.target_text: Sempre que discutimos sobre dinheiro, outros problemas do passado vêm à tona.

examples.en_text: She was afraid that her deepest secrets would come to light.
examples.target_text: Ela tinha medo de que os seus segredos mais profundos viessem à tona.

examples.en_text: New evidence came to light during the police investigation.
examples.target_text: Novas provas vieram à tona durante a investigação da polícia.
